# Component Deep-Dive

Detailed analysis of each Unbound Force tool: purpose, technical details,
maturity, and standalone utility.

## Gaze — Test Quality Analysis

**Purpose**: Static analysis for Go that detects observable side effects and
measures whether tests actually assert on them [11][7].

**Core Innovation**: Contract Coverage — the percentage of *contractual*
side effects (public obligations) that tests verify, as opposed to line
coverage which only tracks execution [11].

### Technical Details

| Aspect | Detail | Source |
|--------|--------|--------|
| Effect types | 37 across 5 tiers (P0-P4) [11] | |
| P0-P2 (implemented) | Return values, error returns, state mutations, I/O, channel sends, file system, DB writes, goroutine spawns, panics, context cancellation [7] | |
| P3-P4 (not implemented) | Stdout/stderr, environment mutations, mutex ops, reflection, unsafe pointers [7] | |
| Metrics | Contract Coverage, Over-Specification Score, GazeCRAP [11] | |
| GazeCRAP formula | complexity² × (1 - contractCoverage)³ + complexity [7] | |
| Assertion accuracy | ~84.7% (target: 90%) [7] | |
| Language | Go 1.25.0+ [22] | |
| Direct deps | 10 (bubbletea, gocyclo, golang.org/x/tools, etc.) [22] | |

### Commands

| Command | Purpose |
|---------|---------|
| `gaze analyze` | Detect all side effects with optional classification [11] |
| `gaze crap` | CRAP scores combining complexity + coverage [11] |
| `gaze quality` | Test quality assessment against contractual effects [11] |
| `gaze report` | AI-powered quality report (Claude or OpenCode adapters) [11] |
| `gaze self-check` | CRAP analysis on Gaze's own source [11] |
| `gaze docscan` | Scan repository for documentation files (JSON output) [11] |
| `gaze schema` | Print JSON Schema for analyze output [11] |
| `gaze init` | Scaffold OpenCode agent and command files [11] |

### Fix Strategy Labels [7]

- `add_tests`: No tests exist
- `add_assertions`: Tests exist but skip contractual effects
- `decompose`: Complexity demands splitting
- `decompose_and_test`: Both issues present

### Standalone Utility

Gaze is the most standalone component. It requires only a Go codebase and
produces JSON output. The `--ai=claude` adapter works outside OpenCode [11].
However, `gaze init` scaffolds OpenCode-specific files [11].

**Key limitation**: Analyzes immediate function bodies only; transitive effects
through called functions are not tracked [7].

## Dewey — Knowledge Graph MCP Server

**Purpose**: Unified knowledge access for AI agents via graph queries and
vector-based semantic search [6][10].

**Origin**: Hard fork of Graphthulhu (skridlevsky, 133 stars, 39 tools) [15],
extended to 48 tools with SQLite persistence, semantic search, pluggable sources,
and knowledge lifecycle management [10].

### Technical Details

| Aspect | Detail | Source |
|--------|--------|--------|
| MCP tools | 48 across 14 categories [10] (12 per website [6]) | |
| Storage | In-memory graph + persistent SQLite at `.uf/dewey/graph.db` [6] | |
| Embeddings | IBM Granite (30M params, 63MB, Apache 2.0) via Ollama [6] | |
| Content sources | 4: local Markdown, GitHub API, web crawl, Go source code [6] | |
| File watching | Real-time via fsnotify [23] | |
| MCP SDK | Official Go SDK v1.2.0 [23] | |
| Direct deps | 8 (MCP SDK, sqlite, fsnotify, html2text, etc.) [23] | |
| Backends | Logseq and Obsidian, both with read-write support [10] | |

### Tool Categories [10]

| Category | Count | Purpose |
|----------|-------|---------|
| Navigate | 6 | Page/block retrieval, link traversal |
| Search | 4 | Full-text, properties, DataScript, tags |
| Analyze | 6 | Graph overview, connections, knowledge gaps |
| Write | 10 | CRUD for pages, blocks, links |
| Decision | 5 | Decision tracking with deadlines |
| Journal | 2 | Date-range journal queries |
| Flashcard | 3 | Spaced repetition (Logseq only) |
| Whiteboard | 2 | Visual connections (Logseq only) |
| Semantic Search | 3 | Vector similarity search |
| Compile | 1 | Synthesize learnings into articles |
| Lint | 1 | Quality issue detection |
| Promote | 1 | Trust tier advancement |
| Indexing | 3 | Source indexing and reindexing |
| Learning | 1 | Store tagged learnings |

### Knowledge Lifecycle [6]

Three lifecycle commands manage content maturity:
- **Compile**: Clusters learnings by topic, synthesizes via LLM
- **Lint**: Detects stale decisions, embedding gaps, contradictions
- **Promote**: draft → validated → authored (requires human review)

### Standalone Utility

Dewey works as a standalone MCP server for any MCP client (Claude Code,
OpenCode, etc.) [9][10]. The main Unbound Force dependency is the trust tier
system and the compilation feature that uses an LLM [6].

## Replicator — Multi-Agent Coordination

**Purpose**: MCP server for coordinating multiple AI coding agents on shared
codebases [9][5].

**Origin**: Go rewrite of cyborg-swarm (TypeScript), originally forked from
swarm-tools by Joel Hooks [9].

### Technical Details

| Aspect | Detail | Source |
|--------|--------|--------|
| MCP tools | 53 across 4 categories [9] | |
| Binary size | ~15MB [9] | |
| Startup time | <50ms [9] | |
| Tests | 190+ [9] | |
| Storage | SQLite WAL mode, 7 tables [9] | |
| Direct deps | 5 (lipgloss, log, termenv, cobra, sqlite) [21] | |
| MCP SDK | Not listed as dependency; likely custom implementation [21] | |

### Tool Categories

Note: Website [5] and README [9] use different category names for the same tools.

| README Name | Website Name | Count | Purpose |
|-------------|-------------|-------|---------|
| Org | Hive | 11 | Work item tracking, epics, sessions |
| Comms | Swarm Mail | 10 | Inter-agent messaging, file reservations |
| Forge | Swarm | 24 | Task decomposition, worktree spawning, review |
| Memory | Memory | 8 | Dewey proxy, learnings storage |

### Key Features [9]

- **Work tracking**: Cell (work item) CRUD, epics, sessions, sync
- **File reservations**: Prevent concurrent edits via messaging system
- **Git worktree isolation**: Per-task isolated working directories
- **Dewey proxy**: HTTP forwarding to Dewey MCP endpoint
- **CLI**: 9 commands (init, setup, serve, cells, doctor, stats, query, docs, version)

### Standalone Utility

Replicator explicitly supports Claude Code via MCP configuration [9]:
```json
{"mcp_servers": {"replicator": {"command": "replicator", "args": ["serve"]}}}
```

However, the embedded agent kit (commands, skills, agents scaffolded by
`replicator init`) is OpenCode-specific [9]. The `ZEN_API_KEY` env var ties
into OpenCode's Zen gateway for LLM calls [9].

## UF CLI — Scaffold Engine

**Purpose**: Distribute the specification framework and agent configuration
into any repository [8].

### Technical Details

| Aspect | Detail | Source |
|--------|--------|--------|
| Binary name | `unbound-force` (alias: `uf`) [8] | |
| Files scaffolded | 50 [8] | |
| Content | Templates, scripts, commands, agents, Divisor review personas, convention packs, OpenSpec schema [8] | |
| Language detection | Auto-detect with `--lang` override [8] | |
| Divisor-only mode | `uf init --divisor` [8] | |
| Distribution | Homebrew tap, RPM [8] | |
| Description | "13 specialized agent personas" [12] | |

### Key Behavior [8]

- User-owned files are skipped on re-run
- Tool-owned files are auto-updated when content changes
- Convention packs are language-specific

## Speckit / OpenSpec — Specification Frameworks

**Speckit** (strategic) [8]:
- 9-phase pipeline for architectural work
- Commands: `/speckit.specify` through `/speckit.implement`
- Includes Constitution governance bridge

**OpenSpec** (tactical) [8]:
- Lightweight workflow for bug fixes and small changes
- Commands: `/opsx:propose` through `/opsx:archive`
- Creates `opsx/<name>` branches with proposal.md, design.md, tasks.md

Both are distributed together via `uf init` [8].

## Gaps and Limitations

- Dewey tool count discrepancy: README says 48 tools across 14 categories [10],
  website says 48 tools across 12 categories [6]. The README enumeration
  (Navigate 6 + Search 4 + Analyze 6 + Write 10 + Decision 5 + Journal 2 +
  Flashcard 3 + Whiteboard 2 + Semantic Search 3 + Compile 1 + Lint 1 +
  Promote 1 + Indexing 3 + Learning 1 = 48) totals 14 categories.
- Replicator category naming inconsistency between website and README [5][9].
- Gaze P3-P4 effect detection is documented as "not yet detected" [7] despite
  gaze being at v1.4.9 [14].
- No published token consumption or cost data for any workflow.
- UF CLI description says "13 specialized agent personas" [12] but only 5 heroes
  are documented [8] — the additional 8 may include review sub-personas and
  workflow-specific agents.
